previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted with acute chest pain and melena. He had a 5-point drop in hematocrit since his recent discharge, where he had been advised to start aspirin. The anemia led to demand ischemia, causing chest pain. He was hemodynamically stable and received two units of packed red blood cells, which improved his hemoglobin. A chest X-ray showed interstitial edema, and he underwent hemodialysis. Upper endoscopy revealed nodular gastritis and an inflammatory polyp, while colonoscopy identified a non-bleeding ulcer in the hepatic flexure; biopsies were taken. Aspirin was discontinued due to GI bleeding risk. Cardiology attributed the chest pain to microvascular ischemia and recommended isosorbide mononitrate and atorvastatin instead. The patient was discharged home with stable vital signs, resolved melena, and plans for outpatient follow-up on biopsy results and pancreatic MRI. He was advised to monitor daily weight and avoid illicit substances.

Brief Hospital Course:
PRIMARY REASON FOR HOSPITALIZATION:
=============================================
___ y/o male with ESRD on HD, AF, and an extensive history of GI 
bleeding, including a recent hospitalization for chest pain and 
BRBPR, presented with chest pain and 2-days of maroon stool.
.
ACTIVE ISSUES:
=============================================
# GI bleed/Acute on chronic blood loss anemia: patient with 
extensive history of previous GI bleeds presented with 3 days of 
maroon stools and 1 day of epigastric pain. Upon admission he 
was hemodynamically stable, with Hct at his baseline of 30. He 
had several episodes of BRBPR during this hospitalization, 
requiring transfusion of pRBCs on 3 occasions, though he always 
remained hemodynamically stable. He underwent upper EGD and 
colonoscopy, which did not show any signs of active bleeding. He 
underwent small capsule endoscopy on ___ that was unsuccessful 
as the capsule was found to be still in his stomach. Repeat KUB 
revealed movement through to large bowel so no further invasive 
intervention needed for removal. Plan for f/u with outpatient 
GI.
.
# Atypical Chest pain: Upon presentation patient had chest pain 
that was atypical, similar to previous episodes he had with GI 
bleeding. Thought to possibly represent demand ischemia, though 
no initial EKG changes, troponin on admission 0.39 (during 
previous hospitalization trops were 0.49-0.53), which may just 
be due to ESRD. His chest pain resolved and did not return.  
Prior to admission the patient had been prescribed isosorbide 
mononitrate for anginal symptoms, though he never filled the 
prescription. He was scheduled for outpatient cardiology 
evaluation to further explore this issue. Additionally, he was 
seen by cardiology consult team during this admission, who 
recommended the option of a beta blocker be explored if it could 
be determined that the patient was no longer using cocaine.
.
# ESRD: T2 diabetes etiology and was continued on his 
___ HD schedule. He was continued on his cinacalcet 
90mg daily, Nephrocaps daily. Had not been taking his sevelamer 
3200mg TID as an outpatient and since not critical per nephro, 
was held for reconsideration on an outpatient basis.
.
# Atrial fibrillation: patient is rate controlled, not on 
anticoagulation (due to recurrent GI bleeding). He was monitored 
on tele. He was initially placed on short acting diltiazem (30mg 
q6hrs) out of concern for active GI bleeding. This was 
eventually uptitrated to his home dose of 90mg q6hrs. He was 
also continued on his home digoxin at 125mcg q48hrs.
.
#T2Diabetes uncontrolled: T2Diabetes with most recent HbA1C of 
9.2% in ___. Complicated by peripheral neuropathy, 
retinopathy. Lantus was held during NPO periods, he was 
maintained on HISS. His home gabapentin was continued.
.
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
===============================================
Transitional issues:
- Would revisit question of outpatient beta blockade therapy
- Consider alternative statin use if patient tolerates
- Patient has several sebaceous cysts (back, right eyebrow) 
which are distressing and bothersome to the patient
- Needs repeat colonoscopy with MAC anesthesia as an outpatient 
with an extended two day prep for transverse polyp removal
- Will likely need repeat small capsule endoscopy as not 
successful as an inpatient
- Held Sevelamer as patient cannot afford copay and has not been 
taking it as an outpatient and not required at this time per 
renal. Revisit need on outpatient basis
